recipe.title: Spinach, Mushroom & Cottage Cheese Shakshuka with Wholemeal Toast
recipe.description: A protein-rich shakshuka with deeply browned mushrooms, spinach and a smoky cumin-tomato sauce, finished with softly set eggs, creamy cottage cheese and crisp wholemeal toast.

ingredients.notes: Whole eggs do not scale perfectly for every serving quantity; round sensibly when scaling.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Use 200 g; carton size may vary.
Use 160 g; retail tub size may vary.

ingredients.preparation: Keep sliced and ready for toasting.
ingredients.notes: Bread slice size varies between products, so nutrition will vary slightly.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Use the entire contents of 1 approximately 400 g tin.

ingredients.preparation: Wash if required and dry thoroughly.

ingredients.notes: Whole onions do not scale perfectly for every serving quantity; round sensibly when scaling.

ingredients.preparation: Peel before finely grating or crushing.

ingredients.notes: Provides gentle background heat rather than making the breakfast strongly spicy.
Sharpens the tomato sauce and balances the dairy richness.
Cottage cheese and bread contribute additional salt.

equipment.notes: Use a broad pan so the mushrooms can brown before the tomato base is added.
Used while the eggs cook so the toast is ready with the shakshuka.

mise_en_place.instruction: Peel the onion, trim the root and stem ends, then dice the usable flesh into approximately 5 mm pieces. Peel and finely grate or crush the garlic. Trim the mushroom stem ends and slice the mushrooms approximately 5 mm thick.
mise_en_place.endpoint: The onion is evenly diced, the garlic is finely prepared and the mushrooms are sliced to a consistent thickness.

mise_en_place.instruction: Wash the spinach if required, then dry it thoroughly. Remove only any unusually thick or damaged stems.
mise_en_place.endpoint: The spinach is clean and dry enough that it will wilt without adding unnecessary water to the sauce.

mise_en_place.instruction: Keep the 2 eggs whole until required. Weigh 200 g liquid egg whites and 160 g cottage cheese into separate ready-to-use portions.
mise_en_place.endpoint: The eggs, egg whites and cottage cheese are ready to add without interrupting cooking.

mise_en_place.instruction: Measure 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp ground cumin, 1/4 tsp chilli flakes, 1/4 tsp fine salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1 tbsp tomato purée and 1 tsp red wine vinegar so they are ready to add in sequence.
mise_en_place.endpoint: All seasoning and sauce ingredients are measured before cooking begins.

procedure.title: Brown the mushrooms and soften the onion
procedure.instruction: Heat the sauté pan over medium-high heat for approximately 1 minute. Add 1 tsp olive oil, followed by the mushrooms and onion. Spread them across the pan and cook for approximately 7-9 minutes, stirring only every 60-90 seconds at first so the mushrooms can release their moisture and develop brown edges.
procedure.endpoint: The mushroom liquid has evaporated, the mushrooms are well browned and the onion is soft with lightly golden edges.

corrective_actions.condition: The mushrooms release liquid and remain grey rather than browning.
corrective_actions.action: Keep the pan uncovered at medium-high heat and avoid stirring until the visible liquid has evaporated.

corrective_actions.condition: The onion begins darkening before the mushrooms have browned.
corrective_actions.action: Reduce the heat slightly and stir more frequently until the mushrooms catch up.

procedure.title: Bloom the garlic, spices and tomato purée
procedure.instruction: Reduce the heat to medium. Add the garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, chilli flakes and tomato purée. Stir continuously for approximately 45-60 seconds, scraping the purée across the base of the pan so it darkens slightly without scorching.
procedure.endpoint: The mixture smells strongly aromatic and the tomato purée has changed from bright red to a slightly darker brick-red colour.

corrective_actions.condition: The garlic or spices begin catching or smelling bitter.
corrective_actions.action: Immediately proceed to the next step and add the canned tomatoes to stop further browning.

procedure.title: Reduce the shakshuka sauce
procedure.instruction: Add the canned tomatoes, 1 tsp red wine vinegar, 1/4 tsp fine salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper. Stir thoroughly and bring to a lively simmer. Cook uncovered over medium heat for approximately 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally and scraping the base of the pan.
procedure.endpoint: The sauce has visibly thickened, a spatula drawn through the centre leaves a trail that remains open for 1-2 seconds, and there is no watery liquid separating around the edges.

corrective_actions.condition: The sauce thickens and catches before the tomatoes have lost their raw canned flavour.
corrective_actions.action: Reduce the heat and add 1 tbsp water, then continue simmering.

corrective_actions.condition: The sauce remains watery after 7 minutes.
corrective_actions.action: Increase the heat slightly and continue uncovered until the stated trail test is achieved.

procedure.title: Wilt the spinach
procedure.instruction: Add the spinach in 2 additions, folding each portion into the hot sauce before adding the next. Cook for approximately 1-2 minutes until all of the spinach has collapsed into the sauce.
procedure.endpoint: The spinach is fully wilted and evenly distributed, while the sauce remains thick rather than watery.

corrective_actions.condition: The spinach releases enough water to loosen the sauce noticeably.
corrective_actions.action: Continue cooking uncovered for another 1-2 minutes until the sauce returns to the previous thick consistency.

procedure.title: Add and set the eggs
procedure.instruction: Reduce the heat to low-medium. Make 2 wells in the sauce and crack 1 egg into each well. Pour the 200 g liquid egg whites evenly into the spaces between the eggs rather than directly over the yolks. Cover the pan and cook for approximately 5-7 minutes.
procedure.endpoint: All egg white, including the added liquid egg white, is fully opaque and set with no translucent patches; the whole-egg yolks may remain soft if preferred.

corrective_actions.condition: The tomato sauce begins bubbling aggressively around the eggs.
corrective_actions.action: Reduce the heat so the eggs set gently rather than becoming tough at the base.

corrective_actions.condition: The egg whites remain translucent after 7 minutes.
corrective_actions.action: Keep the pan covered and continue cooking in 1-minute increments until all white is opaque.

procedure.title: Toast the wholemeal bread
procedure.instruction: While the eggs are setting, toast the 2 slices of wholemeal bread until crisp at the surface and golden at the edges while remaining tender inside.
procedure.endpoint: The toast is hot, crisp and evenly browned without scorched edges.

corrective_actions.condition: The bread is browning too quickly.
corrective_actions.action: Stop the toaster early rather than allowing the edges to burn.

procedure.title: Warm the cottage cheese
procedure.instruction: Once the egg whites are fully set, remove the lid and spoon the cottage cheese in small dollops across the sauce, keeping the egg yolks visible. Cover again for approximately 1 minute over low heat, just until the cottage cheese is warmed but still visibly curded.
procedure.endpoint: The cottage cheese is warm and creamy while retaining distinct curds, and the eggs remain correctly cooked.

corrective_actions.condition: The sauce begins bubbling hard after the cottage cheese is added.
corrective_actions.action: Turn off the heat and allow the residual pan heat to warm the cottage cheese.

plating.instruction: Divide the shakshuka between two warm bowls or shallow plates so each person receives 1 whole egg, approximately half of the extra egg white, vegetables, tomato sauce and cottage cheese. Serve each portion immediately with 1 slice of crisp wholemeal toast for scooping.

storage.storage_instructions: The completed shakshuka is best eaten immediately. If necessary, cool leftovers promptly and refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 1 day. Store toast separately so it does not soften. For make-ahead preparation, the mushroom, spinach and tomato base may be prepared up to 2 days in advance and refrigerated; reheat it until piping hot before adding fresh eggs and cottage cheese.
reheating_methods: Hob: place leftover shakshuka in a covered frying or sauté pan over low heat with 1 tbsp water and heat gently until piping hot throughout, avoiding prolonged heating that will toughen the eggs.
Oven: cover in a suitable ovenproof dish and heat at approximately 170°C until piping hot throughout.
Toast fresh wholemeal bread separately immediately before serving.

either_retailer: Liquid egg whites — 1 carton; use 200 g.
Low-fat cottage cheese — 1 tub; use 160 g.
Wholemeal bread — 1 loaf; use 2 large slices.
Canned chopped tomatoes — 1 approximately 400 g tin.

restaurant_quality_features: Mushrooms are browned until their moisture has evaporated before the tomato sauce is built.
Tomato purée and spices are briefly cooked in the pan to deepen their flavour before liquid is added.
The tomato base is properly reduced so the finished shakshuka is rich rather than watery.
Red wine vinegar supplies controlled acidity to balance the tomatoes, eggs and cottage cheese.
Whole eggs provide rich yolks while additional egg whites raise protein without excessive calories.
Cottage cheese is warmed only briefly so its creamy curd texture remains distinct.
Crisp wholemeal toast provides a contrasting texture and practical way to scoop the thick sauce.
nutrition_notes: Approximately 410 kcal and 38.5 g protein per serving.
Eggs, liquid egg whites and cottage cheese provide the majority of the protein.
Mushrooms, spinach and tomatoes provide substantial vegetable volume for relatively few calories.
Wholemeal toast contributes complex carbohydrate and additional fibre.
Nutrition values are estimates and will vary with the exact cottage cheese, bread and liquid egg-white products used.
critical_success_factors: Brown the mushrooms thoroughly before adding tomato ingredients.
Reduce the tomato sauce until it passes the stated spatula-trail test before adding spinach or eggs.
Cook the added liquid egg whites until fully opaque while avoiding unnecessarily hard whole-egg yolks.
Add the cottage cheese only after the egg whites have set so it retains texture.
Serve immediately with freshly toasted wholemeal bread.
